Consult Summary:
- Young adult female with a 3-day history of a new, severe, constant headache with photophobia and visual “shooting lights,” suspected migraine; face-to-face neurological and ophthalmic examination arranged and analgesic management planned.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Blinding/very severe headache for 3 days, began suddenly on waking.
  - Pain described as diffuse but stronger over the right eye.
  - Photophobia and intermittent visual phenomena described as “shooting lights” or abnormal/flashing vision.
  - No vomiting; patient feels “a bit sick” but has not vomited.
  - No reported weakness, numbness, or tingling.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Onset: started suddenly 3 days prior to consultation.
  - Course: persistent/continuous; partial symptomatic improvement with ibuprofen but pain remains.
  - Severity: patient rates pain as about 8/10 at worst, sometimes down to about 5/10.
  - Sleep: able to sleep; not woken by headache at night; may wake with headache in morning.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Photophobia exacerbates symptoms (bright lights worsen discomfort).
  - Standing up quickly or rapid head movements can cause a stabbing sensation.
  - Ibuprofen provides some relief but does not abolish the pain.
- Associated symptoms / systems review:
  - No fever reported.
  - No cough, sputum, sore throat, ear pain, or sinus pain.
  - No epistaxis or hemoptysis.
  - No change in smell or taste.
  - No recent weight change; some decreased energy attributed to ongoing headache.
  - No recent travel abroad.
- Prior headache history:
  - Occasionally had short headaches previously (e.g., 2 days) relieved by ibuprofen; no prior prolonged severe headaches like current episode.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.
- Remote childhood episode of head pain with no identified cause (resolved).
- Medications:
  - Combined oral contraceptive ("the pill") — started approximately 1 year ago; name/dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Ibuprofen taken PRN for headache — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies:
  - No known drug allergies (patient reports none).

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Employment: works from home; recent headaches have impaired ability to work (missed one full day, limited productivity on other days).
- Tobacco: denies smoking.
- Alcohol: consumes alcohol; patient estimate “probably like three, once a week” (amount/frequency imprecise).
- Recreational drugs: denies other drug use.

Family History:
- Mother has recurrent migraines, reportedly severe with vomiting.
- No other family medical history provided.

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs documented.
- No physical examination was performed during this remote consult.
- Plan made to perform neurological examination and fundoscopy at in-person appointment.

Investigations:
- No investigations, imaging, or laboratory results documented.
- Planned: in-person neurological examination and fundoscopy; blood pressure check at appointment.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute severe headache (clinical impression: possible migraine)
  - Assessment: New-onset, severe, persistent headache for 3 days with photophobia and visual phenomena, consistent with possible migraine; cannot rule out other causes without examination.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange face-to-face appointment for full neurological examination and fundoscopy (support team to book; patient advised appointment can be cancelled if symptoms resolve).
    - Prescribe a stronger analgesic in place of ibuprofen (medication name/dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript); advise to take with food.
    - Paracetamol may be used concomitantly (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Advise patient to attend Emergency Department (A&E) if headache becomes unbearable, worsens, or changes character.
    - Provide telephone contact for further advice if needed.
- Issue 2: Contraceptive safety in context of possible migraine
  - Assessment: Patient is on an oral contraceptive started ~1 year ago; discussion that some contraceptives may be inappropriate if migraine with aura is confirmed.
  - Plan:
    - Check blood pressure at the in-person appointment.
    - If neurological exam and history confirm migraine with aura (e.g., recurrent visual aura), consider contraceptive review/change; continue current pill for now.
- Issue 3: Functional impact / work
  - Assessment: Headache has impaired ability to work from home, resulted in missed work.
  - Plan:
    - Address functional impact during in-person visit; manage symptoms and provide further occupation-related advice/documentation if required.

General plan items:
- Book an in-person consultation for examination and BP measurement via support team.
- Cancel appointment if symptoms fully settle before scheduled visit.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No recorded vital signs (blood pressure, pulse, temperature).
  - No formal neurological examination findings or fundoscopy results.
  - No medication names, doses, routes, or frequencies documented for the analgesic the clinician intended to prescribe.
  - Specific type/name of oral contraceptive not documented.
  - No laboratory/imaging results.
  - No formal assessment of visual acuity or a formal description of the visual phenomena beyond patient report.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - None identified (no contradictory statements), aside from some imprecise phrasing regarding alcohol intake and an omitted contraceptive name.
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Initial audio difficulty; several brief inaudible/blank responses where the patient did not state the pill name and a few phrases were unclear. Overall history obtained but lacking specific medication and vital sign details.
